es: Distinguir causa, correlación y posibilidad con el verbo adecuado (causes, is linked to, may account for) y corregir causas exageradas.

teaching.en: Heavy rain causes the river to flood, so rain is the cause of the damage.
teaching.es: La lluvia fuerte hace que el río se desborde, así que la lluvia es la causa del daño.
teaching.explanationEs: Causes, leads to y results in afirman una causa ya comprobada.
segments: Heavy rain causes the river to flood, so
rain is the cause of the damage.
teaching.audioText: Heavy rain causes the river to flood, so rain is the cause of the damage.

teaching.en: Too little sleep leads to poor results, and several studies confirm the trend.
teaching.es: Dormir poco provoca malos resultados, y varios estudios confirman la tendencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Leads to + sustantivo: A provoca B; trend = tendencia que se repite.
segments: Too little sleep leads to poor results,
and several studies confirm the trend.
teaching.audioText: Too little sleep leads to poor results, and several studies confirm the trend.

teaching.en: Reading for pleasure is linked to higher exam marks, but a link is not proof.
teaching.es: Leer por placer se relaciona con mejores notas de examen, pero una relación no es una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Is linked to describe dos cosas que van juntas, sin decir cuál provoca cuál.
segments: Reading for pleasure is linked to higher exam
marks, but a link is not proof.
teaching.audioText: Reading for pleasure is linked to higher exam marks, but a link is not proof.

teaching.en: There is a strong correlation between ice cream sales and swimming accidents.
teaching.es: Hay una fuerte correlación entre las ventas de helados y los accidentes al nadar.
teaching.explanationEs: Correlation between X and Y: con between … and, no con of.
segments: There is a strong correlation between
ice cream sales and swimming accidents.
teaching.audioText: There is a strong correlation between ice cream sales and swimming accidents.

teaching.en: Hot weather may account for both figures; ice cream is not necessarily the cause.
teaching.es: El calor puede explicar ambas cifras; el helado no es necesariamente la causa.
teaching.explanationEs: May account for expresa una explicación posible; not necessarily = no tiene por qué.
segments: Hot weather may account for both figures;
ice cream is not necessarily the cause.
teaching.audioText: Hot weather may account for both figures; ice cream is not necessarily the cause.

teaching.en: It could be a coincidence that there was a rise in both during the same summer.
teaching.es: Podría ser una casualidad que hubiera un aumento en ambos durante el mismo verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Could/may/might + be marcan duda; coincidence = casualidad; rise = aumento.
segments: It could be a coincidence that there was
a rise in both during the same summer.
teaching.audioText: It could be a coincidence that there was a rise in both during the same summer.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe una relación sin afirmar causa.

choices.text: Owning a dog is linked to lower stress in this survey.
Owning a dog causes lower stress in every home.
Owning a dog leads to lower stress, and that is proved.

feedback.es: Is linked to describe una relación observada en una encuesta; causes y leads to afirman una causa.

hint.es: Busca el verbo que solo dice que dos cosas van juntas.

prompt.es: Completa: «El retraso puede explicar las ventas bajas.»

feedback.es: Un modal de posibilidad seguido de account for presenta una explicación posible, no segura.

hint.es: Necesitas un modal que exprese posibilidad.

origin.text: The delay ___ account for the low sales.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hay una correlación entre el sueño y las notas.»

answer.text: There is a correlation between sleep and marks

feedback.es: La correlación se construye con between … and, y aquí no dice que uno cause al otro.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que afirma una causa probada.

choices.text: Heavy traffic is linked to air pollution in this city.
Heavy traffic causes air pollution, and tests confirm it.
Heavy traffic may account for some of the air pollution.

feedback.es: Causes junto con la confirmación de las pruebas expresa una causa; las otras dos son relación y posibilidad.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hubo un aumento en ambos casos, pero podría ser una casualidad.»

feedback.es: Could be a coincidence reconoce que dos aumentos pueden coincidir por azar.

origin.text: There was a rise in both cases, but it could be a ___.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concluye el locutor.

choices.text: Rain may explain both, so there is no direct cause.

feedback.es: El locutor propone que la lluvia explique ambos aumentos, así que no hay causa directa entre ellos.

origin.audio: Sales of umbrellas go up when the number of colds goes up. That does not mean umbrellas give people colds. The rain may account for both.

prompt.es: Completa: causa comprobada en la primera frase, relación en la segunda.

feedback.es: La primera frase afirma una causa con leads to; la segunda solo vincula dos datos con linked to.

sentences: Too much sugar ___ to health problems, and studies confirm it.
Being tall is ___ to playing football, but it is not the only factor.

prompt.es: Suaviza esta causa exagerada con una relación y un modal de duda.

answer.text: Video games may be linked to lower marks in teenagers.
accepted: Video games may be linked to lower marks in teenagers.
Video games might be associated with bad marks in teenagers.
There may be a correlation between video games and bad marks in teens.

feedback.es: Una causa exagerada se corrige con is linked to, is associated with o correlation, más may, might o could.

origin.text: Titular exagerado: Video games cause bad marks in teenagers.

prompt.es: Elige la versión más prudente del titular.

choices.text: Cold weather may be linked to more colds.
Cold weather is the cause of every cold.

feedback.es: La versión prudente usa may be linked to; always causes y the cause of every son exageraciones.

origin.text: Titular original: Cold weather causes colds.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo presenta la locutora el papel de las luces.

choices.text: The lights are the proved cause of the fall.
The lights are possibly one factor among several.
The lights have no link with the fall at all.

feedback.es: La locutora dice que las luces podrían explicar parte de la bajada y que otros factores también importan.

origin.audio: The city says accidents fell after the new lights were installed. That is a correlation, not proof. The lights might account for part of the fall, but other factors may matter too.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El aumento puede explicar ambas tendencias.»

answer.text: The rise may account for both trends

feedback.es: May account for presenta el aumento como explicación posible de las dos tendencias.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con lo que afirma.

feedback.es: Leads to afirma causa, is linked to solo relaciona y might account for deja una explicación posible.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta sobre una correlación.

choices.text: There is a strong correlation of age and salary.
There is a strong correlation among age to salary.
There is a strong correlation between age and salary.

feedback.es: Correlation se combina con between … and; of y among … to no funcionan.
